_how_to_use: PASTE ONLY THE `prompt` FIELD INTO THE IMAGE MODEL. Nothing else in this file is for the model. Pasting the whole file produced a collage of several captioned slides, because `renditions_wanted` lists two sizes, `framing.aspect_ratios` lists two ratios, and headline_in_app / caption_in_app are text - the model read all of that as a brief to draw multiple frames with words on them. Those fields are for the render pipeline and for whoever writes the app copy.
_source_image_note: Save the image you keep in this folder named `01_welcome_1_live_classes` with whatever extension the model gave you - .jpg, .png, .jpeg and .webp are all accepted. Only the NAME has to match this file; the extension does not. lessons/scripts/tutor_images.py then renders it to renders/01_welcome_1_live_classes/ as slide_1080x1920 (9:16 phone slide) and card_1080x1350 (4:5). Renditions are always written as PNG regardless of the source format.
audience: a parent or guardian setting up for a learner
caption_in_app: Follow the subject's expert and simplifier through CAPS-aligned lessons - live, then yours to rewatch.
intent: the parent seeing that real teaching happens on a schedule
prompt: A single photograph, one continuous scene, filling the whole frame. A Black South African father in his forties standing behind his seated son at a dining table in the evening, both looking at a tablet standing in a small folding stand on the table, the stand clearly visible under it - screen angled away from camera, nothing readable. His hand rests lightly on the back of the chair. Warm indoor light. He is watching his son, not the screen: this is about reassurance, not supervision. photorealistic documentary photograph, natural available light, real skin texture, candid and unposed, shot on a full-frame camera, 35mm, f/2.8, true-to-life colour.
negative_prompt: any text, letters, numbers, words, signage, logos, watermarks, user-interface elements, phone screens showing apps, charts or graphs, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, plastic sheen, cinematic colour grade, film still look, motion blur, lens flare, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted faces, stock-photo smiles, American classrooms, generic 'African' styling, collage, multiple panels, split screen, side-by-side frames, contact sheet, grid of images, storyboard, several phone mockups, device frames, app screenshots, before-and-after, picture-in-picture, borders, margins, framed print, device floating in mid-air, phone standing on nothing, tablet balanced impossibly upright, no visible support, object hovering

_pipeline_only._note: NOT model input - read by the render script and the app.

framing.composition: subject in the lower two thirds, calm uncluttered space in the upper third where the slide's headline and caption sit - the image must never compete with the copy
framing.safe_area: keep the top 28% and bottom 18% visually quiet: the headline sits above, the button below

_support_note: The device rests on something NAMED. 'Propped-up' describes the result, not the support, so the model rendered a phone standing upright on nothing (owner, 2026-07-30). A stack of exercise books or a cheap folding stand is both plausible in a South African home and something the model can actually draw in contact with the device.
_casting_note: Cast to complete the spread across the branch.
